key_insight: Strain can strongly tune electron and hole g-factors in bulk CsPbX3 perovskites, even driving them through zero, while nanocrystals are much less strain-sensitive because of quantum confinement.
engineering_relevance: This suggests strain engineering as a practical knob for spintronic and magneto-optical control in lead-halide perovskite devices, especially where bulk-like behavior is accessible.
method: Built an 18-band k·p model for cubic CsPbX3.
Parametrized the model using DFT target band structures.
Used linear response theory and real-space calculations to evaluate g-factors under external strain in bulk and nanocrystals.
evidence_signal: The study is theoretical, combining DFT-calibrated band-structure modeling with computed g-factor trends under strain, rather than experimental device measurements.
watch_item: The results are specific to the reference cubic phase and modeled nanocrystal sizes/conditions, so real devices may deviate due to phase instability, defects, and morphology effects.
paper_title: Strain tunability of electron and hole g-factors in CsPb$X_3$: bulk and nanocrystals
